SILENCE

In this new land of mine
I am to speak no more;
My tongue is wrapped in twine
To be untwisted when I know
It shall not twist or tie again.
The hand that once so well
Could move a knife or pen
Is stilled by hands unseen
That clutch it now and keep
Its strings from twisting into knots.
For speech has died away,
Speech never heard before.
Only my tears betray
A pain unuttered yet,
And silence reigns above me here.

SAITH

There was a great feast of drinking goblets in old days
At Elfinland's borders, as is told by me;
But now they are all buried, far down in the ground,
And but their names remain written on stone.
All were made with wondrous cunning out of the mountain-stone,
Or wrought by elves from silver or gold;
So that if one should ask it who fashioned them, then
The answer would be "elves" to every bold!

LXXVII

Waiting by a river in a noonday sun
By an old bridge one afternoon I stood;
I looked down on my soul’s great water run
Over stones that were once broken bones of men,
And saw it change as the hour turned noon;
Then there was silence through all nature so profound,
That when a bell rang out from some cathedral town
The sound seemed lost to every voice but mine.
What shall I say? what shall I call this pain?
Or where shall I go seeking a name for it?
Is it sorrow?

Not even one little primrose peep through the leaves?

And not a single bird has come from southern climes--

From rice they brew a liquid food

To help us welcome happiness.
